platform.definition: The area beside the tracks where passengers board or leave metro trains.

tunnel.definition: An underground or covered passage through which the railway runs.

track.definition: The rails and supporting structure on which a metro train runs.

escalator.definition: Moving stairs that carry people between floors.

elevator.definition: A machine that carries people or goods up and down between floors.
elevator.exampleUsage: Omar asks whether the elevator is available for his route.

turnstile.definition: A gate consisting of a post that acts as a pivot for rotating arms.

mezzanine.definition: An intermediate floor between the main floors of a station or building.

concourse.definition: A large open area in a station through which passengers move.

entrance.definition: A route or opening used to enter a station.

exit.definition: A doorway or route used to leave the station.

car.definition: One passenger carriage forming part of a metro train.

seat.definition: A place designed for one person to sit.

handrail.definition: A fixed rail that passengers hold for support or balance.

pole.definition: An upright bar that standing passengers can hold for support.

map.definition: A drawing that shows places, routes, and geographical features.

emergency-brake.definition: A control used to request or activate an emergency stop on a train.

connecting-door.definition: A door between connected train cars that allows authorized movement from one car to another where permitted.
connecting-door.exampleUsage: The connecting door remained closed while the train was moving.

ticket-machine.definition: A self-service machine that sells or issues public-transport tickets.
ticket-machine.exampleUsage: Passengers used the ticket machine before entering the platform.

metro-card.definition: A stored-value or travel card used to pay fares on a metro or other public-transport system.
metro-card.exampleUsage: Omar asks which actual metro cards this operator accepts.

tap.definition: To briefly place a travel card near or against a reader to record a journey.

fare.definition: The price paid for a journey on public transport.

gate.definition: A barrier controlling entry to a station or fare-paid area.

top-up.definition: To add enough of something to restore it to the level needed, especially money or credit in an account.

single-ride.definition: A ticket or fare valid for one journey on a transport system.
single-ride.exampleUsage: A single-ride ticket is valid for one trip.

weekly-pass.definition: A transport pass that allows specified travel for one week.
weekly-pass.exampleUsage: Maya checks the weekly pass’s dates and coverage.

monthly-pass.definition: A transport pass that allows specified travel for about one month.
monthly-pass.exampleUsage: His monthly pass covers regular subway journeys.

contactless.definition: Describing a supported card or device communicating near a reader without a wired connection for payment or validation.
contactless.exampleUsage: Omar asks whether his card supports contactless payment.

line-map.definition: A diagram showing the routes, stations, and connections of a transit system.
line-map.exampleUsage: The line map helped passengers find the transfer station.

direction-sign.definition: A sign that shows travelers which way to reach a destination or continue along a route.

exit-sign.definition: A sign showing the direction of a way out.
exit-sign.exampleUsage: The exit sign pointed toward the street stairs.

transfer-sign.definition: A sign showing where passengers can change from one route or service to another.
transfer-sign.exampleUsage: The transfer sign pointed toward the green line.

platform-number.definition: A number used to identify a particular train platform.
platform-number.exampleUsage: The display showed platform number four.

next-train.definition: The train scheduled to arrive or depart after the current time.
next-train.exampleUsage: The screen showed the arrival time of the next train.

last-train.definition: The final scheduled train service of the day on a route.
last-train.exampleUsage: The notice displayed the time of the last train.

gap-warning.definition: A safety message warning passengers about the space between a train and the platform edge.
gap-warning.exampleUsage: A gap warning reminded passengers to watch their step.

no-smoking.definition: A rule or sign showing that smoking is not allowed in an area.
no-smoking.exampleUsage: A no-smoking sign was posted on the platform.

emergency.definition: A sudden unforeseen crisis (usually involving danger) that requires immediate action.

commuter.definition: A person regularly travelling between home and work or study, not necessarily every day.
commuter.arabicTranslation: شخص يتنقل بانتظام للعمل أو الدراسة

tourist.definition: A person who travels for pleasure.

busker.definition: A person who entertains people for money in public places (as by singing or dancing), usually while asking for money.

vendor.definition: A person who promotes or exchanges goods or services for money.

guard.definition: A worker responsible for safety and security at the station.

conductor.definition: A train crew member who assists passengers and may check tickets.

cleaner.definition: A worker who cleans trains or station areas.

crowd.definition: A large number of things or people considered together.

rush-hour.definition: It refers to the periods at the start and end of the workday when large numbers of people commute.

queue.definition: A line of people waiting for their turn.

yellow-line.definition: A yellow safety line marking an area passengers should remain behind near a platform edge.
yellow-line.exampleUsage: Passengers waited behind the yellow line.

cctv.definition: A CCTV installation consists of cameras, recording devices, and related equipment serving a specific location.
cctv.exampleUsage: A CCTV camera monitors part of the concourse.

emergency-phone.definition: A phone provided for contacting urgent assistance, indoors or outdoors.
emergency-phone.exampleUsage: The emergency phone is provided for contacting urgent assistance.

fire-extinguisher.definition: A portable or fixed device that releases a suitable substance to put out or contain a small fire.
fire-extinguisher.exampleUsage: The fire extinguisher remains in its designated place.

defibrillator.definition: A device delivering an electric shock to treat certain dangerous heart rhythms when appropriate.
defibrillator.exampleUsage: A defibrillator is installed near the help point.

help-point.definition: A fixed station where passengers can contact staff or emergency assistance.
help-point.exampleUsage: She used the help point to ask station staff for directions.

alarm.definition: A sound, signal or system warning of danger.

barrier.definition: A gate or obstacle that controls access or separates areas.

evacuation-sign.definition: A sign showing an emergency exit route or evacuation direction.
evacuation-sign.exampleUsage: The evacuation sign pointed toward the emergency stairs.

first-aid-kit.definition: A collection of supplies for initial care of an injury or illness.

door.definition: A movable panel allowing entry to or exit from a train car.
door.exampleUsage: The door opens for boarding while the train is stationary.

window.definition: A glazed opening allowing a view outside a train car.

speaker.definition: A device producing announcements or other sound.
speaker.exampleUsage: An announcement plays through the speaker.
